headline: PLS.AX rockets nearly 10% on a bullish lithium swing while the ASX 200 surges to 8,804 — a strong day across the board except for oil and Microsoft.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a cracking session today, jumping nearly 10% to $6.52. Lithium sentiment has been turning — GM reportedly rethinking its preference for cheaper LFP battery chemistry in favour of lithium, and analysts are flagging a potential supply deficit ahead. That kind of bullish shift gets lithium miners like Pilbara moving fast.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: A solid day for the AI ETF, up nearly 3% to $17.41. The broader AI infrastructure boom is getting attention on the ASX, and last night's strong NASDAQ rally — up 2.5% — gave global AI stocks a nice tailwind that flowed through today.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout laggard last night, dropping 1.77% to $390.34 while the rest of the NASDAQ surged. There's growing chatter that investors are reassessing Microsoft's AI spending versus actual returns — the market seems to be favouring Google's story right now, where AI price cuts are seen as a competitive strength rather than a margin risk.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a good day, up 1.33% to $76.20. As a diversified fund with heavy exposure to global and Australian shares, it rode the wave of the ASX 200's near-2% surge today.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up 1.22% today to $519.67, reflecting last night's strong US session where the S&P 500 gained 1.75%. The ETF tracks the entire US market, so a broad-based rally there flows straight through.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.03% today to $8.63. Crude oil (WTI) dropped $1.63 to $86.08 last night — OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast again, which spooked energy markets. Lower expected oil demand means lower expected earnings for the energy companies inside this ETF.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google edged up 0.92% last night to $356.56. The market liked Google's aggressive AI pricing moves — they've been cutting API costs sharply, putting real pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic. Investors seem to see this as Google playing to win the enterprise AI race.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two ticked up 0.77% last night to $212.08, riding the general NASDAQ lift. No specific company news driving this — it's broadly moving with the market.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.46% today to $91.32. Emerging markets got a gentle boost from the stronger AUD and positive global risk sentiment, though the move was modest compared to the broader market rally.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — hold after a massive single-day move
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped nearly 10% today to $6.52. The lithium narrative is turning bullish — GM reconsidering LFP battery preference, supply deficit talk heating up — but a 10% single-day spike often invites a pullback. You're still slightly underwater overall (-3.26%). Hold and watch for follow-through next week before adding.

watch_today.title: MSFT — underperforming while NASDAQ rips
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 1.77% last night while the NASDAQ gained 2.54%. That's a meaningful divergence. The market seems worried that Microsoft's heavy AI investment isn't converting to revenue fast enough, especially as Google slashes its AI pricing. You're down 11.91% overall on this position. No reason to panic, but worth watching if it keeps lagging when the broader market is strong.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF picking up steam
watch_today.detail: GXAI jumped 2.96% today to $17.41, its best day in a while. The NASDAQ's 2.54% surge last night plus growing attention on ASX AI ETFs is providing real momentum. You're still down 8.51% overall, but the trend is improving. Hold and let the AI infrastructure theme do its work.

watch_today.title: RBA decision Monday — rate hold expected, but watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: The RBA meets on Tuesday 16 June and a Reuters poll of economists points firmly to a hold at 4.35%. Several banks have already cut home loan rates ahead of the decision, anticipating the RBA is done hiking. If you're on a variable mortgage or considering refinancing, this week is a good time to shop around — some banks are moving before the official call.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — oil headwinds from OPEC demand cuts
watch_today.detail: OPEC has cut its 2026 global oil demand growth forecast again, sending crude down to $86 a barrel last night. This is a structural headwind for FUEL.AX, which holds global energy companies. There's a counter-narrative — Rystad Energy is warning oil could spike to $150 if Iran conflict escalates — but for now the trend is soft. Hold unless you have a specific view on geopolitical risk.

watch_today.title: GOOG — AI price war is a tailwind, not a threat
watch_today.detail: Google's aggressive cuts to its AI model pricing (Gemini API) are rattling OpenAI and Anthropic but being read positively by the market — Google rose 0.92% last night. As a GOOG holder, this is good news: lower prices drive higher adoption, and Google has the scale to absorb the margin hit better than its rivals.

markets.summary: A strong day all round. The ASX 200 closed up 1.98% at 8,804 — a big move for a single session. Last night in the US, the NASDAQ surged 2.54% and the S&P 500 gained 1.75%, so the local market had plenty of momentum to ride. Gold had an exceptional night, jumping 2.65% to $4,199 USD/oz — investors are piling in as a safe haven amid global uncertainty. Oil was the odd one out, falling 1.86% to $86.08 after OPEC trimmed its demand forecasts. The Aussie dollar strengthened slightly to 70.3 US cents, which is worth keeping in mind — a stronger AUD slightly reduces the local value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back.

politics.summary: The big local story is the RBA — markets and homeowners are watching Tuesday's rate decision closely, with economists expecting a hold at 4.35%. Meanwhile, the NDIS shake-up is causing a stoush between Canberra and the states.

stories.title: RBA expected to hold rates at 4.35% on June 16 — but relief is coming
stories.why_it_matters: A Reuters poll of economists is firmly pointing to the RBA holding the cash rate at 4.35% at Tuesday's meeting. However, multiple banks have already jumped ahead of the decision and cut their home loan rates — suggesting the market believes the rate hiking cycle is done. The AFR is reporting the RBA itself sees the housing market facing tax 'headwinds'. If you're a homeowner or have a variable mortgage, the direction of travel is improving even if Tuesday brings no change.

stories.title: Banks cutting home loan rates ahead of RBA decision
stories.why_it_matters: Several of Australia's major banks are cutting home loan interest rates before the RBA even meets, betting the central bank is finished with rate hikes. This is unusual — banks typically wait for the RBA to move first. It signals strong confidence in the market that borrowing costs have peaked, which is good news for homeowners and property investors, though it also reflects weak housing demand that banks are trying to stimulate.

stories.title: States warn federal government: we can't replace NDIS services for those cut off
stories.why_it_matters: State disability ministers have publicly lashed the Albanese government's overhaul of the NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme), which is removing some participants from the scheme. The states are warning they simply don't have the funding or services to pick up the slack for people who get cut. This is a politically sensitive fight — the federal government says the scheme needed to be reined in financially, but states say vulnerable people will fall through the cracks without a proper alternative.

ai.summary: The AI pricing war is heating up fast — Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are slashing prices to grab market share. Meanwhile, regulators around the world are scrambling to catch up, and Anthropic's CEO is warning about weapons-grade risk if AI goes unregulated.

stories.title: Google slashes AI prices, putting OpenAI and Anthropic under real pressure
stories.why_it_matters: Google has dramatically cut the cost of using its Gemini AI models via API (the way businesses plug AI into their apps). This is forcing OpenAI and Anthropic to respond with their own cuts, kicking off what looks like a full-blown price war. For GOOG shareholders, this is a calculated power move — Google has the infrastructure scale to win a price war that could squeeze smaller rivals. For businesses using AI tools, cheaper access means faster adoption.

stories.title: Trump signs new AI executive order — could change how top models are launched
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has signed a new AI executive order that could require OpenAI, Google and Anthropic to follow new rules around how and when they release AI models to the public. The details are still emerging, but it signals the US federal government is stepping in to shape AI development — something that could slow certain model releases or require more safety testing before launch. This adds regulatory uncertainty for US AI companies, including Google.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO warns unregulated AI could become a 'weapon of mass destruction'
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic's CEO (maker of the Claude AI) has issued a stark public warning that without proper regulation, AI systems could be weaponised at a scale comparable to weapons of mass destruction. This is notable because it's coming from inside the industry — not from an outside critic. The timing coincides with Trump's new AI order and global regulatory scrambles in the EU, Canada and Latin America, all of which are trying to put guardrails on AI development.

stories.title: Anthropic blindsides its business partners with surprise move
stories.why_it_matters: The Information is reporting that Anthropic made a surprise move that caught its business partners off guard — though full details aren't public yet. In the context of the AI pricing war and the new regulatory environment, any sudden strategic shifts from a major AI player are worth watching. It could relate to pricing, model access terms, or partnerships.

stories.title: Claude Fable 5 vs GPT 5.5 vs Gemini 3.1 Pro — the AI model race heats up
stories.why_it_matters: The next generation of frontier AI models is hitting the market almost simultaneously — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, OpenAI's GPT 5.5, and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro are all in the race. This is the sharp end of the AI competition and it's moving fast. For investors in GOOG or GXAI.AX, this arms race is the core driver of value — whoever wins model performance benchmarks tends to win enterprise contracts.

sport.summary: The Rabbitohs absolutely demolished the Broncos last night in an emotional Round 15 opener, and the AFL finals race is getting tight with eight clubs still fighting for spots.

stories.title: Rabbitohs thrash Broncos 48-6 in emotional Jai Arrow tribute game
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney put in a stunning performance last night at Accor Stadium, hammering the Broncos 48-6. The game was charged with emotion around Jai Arrow, who had the crowd in tears (Arrow has been dealing with personal hardship). Alex Johnston was reportedly electric, bringing fans to their feet. For the Broncos, this was their biggest halftime deficit in the club's history — a shocking result.

stories.title: Dolphins vs Roosters tonight at Suncorp — Gold Coast local interest
stories.why_it_matters: Tonight's big game is Dolphins vs Roosters at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, kicking off at 8:00 PM. Worth watching if you're a Gold Coast local with an eye on the Queensland teams — the Dolphins are fighting for finals relevance in Round 15.

stories.title: SA locks in AFL Gather Round until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia has locked in hosting the AFL's Gather Round festival until 2029, though no decision has been made yet on which venues will be used. Gather Round — where all 18 AFL teams play in one location over a long weekend — has become one of the calendar's marquee events. Adelaide locked it in for at least three more years, good news for SA tourism and the AFL's innovation agenda.

stories.title: Eight clubs in frantic fight for last four AFL finals spots
stories.why_it_matters: With the AFL season past the halfway mark, eight clubs are still genuinely fighting for the last four finals positions. Fox Sports describes the battle as a race to avoid 'no man's land' — the dreaded mid-table finish where you're too good to get a top draft pick but too bad to make finals. Expect the next four rounds to be high-stakes footy across the competition.
